subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Auto-Enrollment in Retirement
description: A 60-second lesson on Auto-Enrollment in Retirement.

hook.text: At companies with opt-in retirement plans, 49% of employees enroll. Switch to auto-enroll and participation jumps.

buildup.text: Madrian and Shea's landmark study showed that changing from opt-in to opt-out nearly doubled saving rates.

discovery.text: Employees didn't study the plan or calculate returns. They just accepted whatever was set up for them. Inertia rules.

twist.text: Auto-enrollment at 3% means many save too little. The Save More Tomorrow program auto-escalates contributions over time.

climax.text: A default contribution rate is more powerful than any financial literacy program.

punchline.text: Don't teach better choices. Default them.

quiz.question: What happened when retirement plans switched from opt-in to opt-out?
options: Enrollment dropped because people felt forced

details.summary: Auto-enrollment in retirement savings changes the default from opting in to opting out, dramatically increasing participation rates. Instead of requiring employees to actively sign up, they are enrolled automatically and must take action to leave the plan.
details.whyItMatters: Auto-enrollment is the most successful nudge ever implemented at scale. Participation in retirement savings jumps from around 40 percent under opt-in to over 90 percent under auto-enrollment, transforming retirement security for millions without.
takeaways: Switching from opt-in to opt-out raises retirement plan participation from 40 to 90 percent
People who are auto-enrolled tend to stay at the default contribution rate
Auto-escalation combines with auto-enrollment to increase savings rates over time

faq.question: Why does auto-enrollment work so much better than opt-in?
faq.answer: Three forces align: inertia means people stick with whatever requires no action; the default feels like an implicit recommendation; and procrastination means people who intend to enroll often delay indefinitely under opt-in. Auto-enrollment leverages all three.

faq.question: What is the main critique of auto-enrollment as a nudge?
faq.answer: People tend to stick at the default contribution rate, which is often set low to minimize opt-outs. This means auto-enrollment locks in low savings rates. Auto-escalation, which automatically increases contributions over time, addresses this limitation.
